notes: {{PICT}} is replaced with the path of a PICT 3.7.4 binary that is NOT on PATH. Evals without {{PICT}} run on a machine where PICT cannot be found. Executors cannot ask follow-up questions; anything they would ask goes into their reply.

evals.name: derive-from-user-story
evals.prompt:
Here's the story for our new export feature, can you work out a sensible set of test cases? We obviously can't test every combination.

---
As a user I can export the orders list. Formats: CSV, XLSX or PDF. I can export the current page, my selected rows, or all rows matching the filter. I choose whether column headers are included (not applicable to PDF, which always has them). The file can be downloaded directly or sent to my email. Exports of more than 10,000 rows are always delivered by email, never as a direct download. PDF export is limited to 5,000 rows; above that the PDF option is disabled. Admins can additionally include the internal 'margin' column; regular users never see that option.
---

PICT is available at {{PICT}} (it's not on my PATH). Put the files in the output folder.
evals.expected_output: A PICT model derived from the story (format, scope, headers, delivery, row count with boundaries around 5,000 and 10,000, role, margin column) with constraints for the stated rules, generated by the real PICT binary, presented as an annotated table with assumptions listed.
expectations: A .pict model file and a .tsv output file are saved in the outputs folder
The saved .tsv is exactly what PICT produces for the saved .pict model (verified by rerunning PICT)
The model includes row-count values on both sides of the 5,000 and the 10,000 thresholds

Each of the four stated rules (headers not applicable to PDF, over 10,000 rows email only, PDF unavailable above 5,000 rows, margin column only for admins) is either encoded as a constraint or explicitly covered as an expected result in the test cases
The reply lists the assumptions or open questions made while deriving the model
The reply states the number of generated test cases together with the exhaustive count for comparison
The reply does not invent expected results that the story does not state

evals.name: dependency-rules
evals.prompt:
I need combinatorial test cases for our subscription signup. Options:

- Plan: Free, Pro, Enterprise
- Billing cycle: monthly or annual (Free has no billing at all)
- Seats: 1, 5, 50, 500
- SSO: on/off
- Support: community, email, priority
- Region: US, EU, APAC

Rules from the pricing doc:
1. Free is limited to exactly 1 seat.
2. Pro allows up to 50 seats.
3. SSO can only be enabled on Enterprise.
4. Priority support is only sold with annual billing, and never on Free.
5. Free only gets community support.

PICT lives at {{PICT}} (not on PATH). Save everything to the output folder.
evals.expected_output: A model with correct constraints for all five rules plus billing-not-applicable for Free, every value still reachable, table generated by PICT, no rule dropped or loosened.
expectations: A .pict model file and a .tsv output file are saved in the outputs folder
The saved .tsv is exactly what PICT produces for the saved .pict model (verified by rerunning PICT)
PICT accepts the saved model with exit code 0 and prints no warnings on standard error
No generated row violates rule 1 or 2: Free rows have 1 seat, Pro rows have at most 50 seats
No generated row violates rule 3: SSO is on only in Enterprise rows
No generated row violates rule 4 or 5: priority support appears only with annual billing and never on Free; Free rows have community support
Free rows carry a not-applicable billing value, and no non-Free row does
Every value declared in the model appears in at least one generated row
